problem:
A database is being scanned by cleanup software. The rate at which the number of unprocessed records decays $R(t),$ after $t$ minutes, can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}R}{\text{d}t}=-0.25R.
$$

If there are $20\,000$ unprocessed records at the start of the scan, how many minutes does it take for the number of unprocessed records to decrease to $1\,000?$ Round your answer to the nearest minute.
worked_solution:
We model the number of unprocessed records using the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}R}{\text{d}t}=-0.25R.
$$

The solution to this equation is

$$
R(t)={R}_{0}\,{e}^{-0.25t},
$$

where ${R}_{0}$ is the initial number of unprocessed records.

We're told that there are $20\,000$ unprocessed records at the start of the scan, so we have ${R}_{0}=20\,000.$

Let ${t}_{1}$ be the time when the number of unprocessed records has decreased to $1\,000.$ That is,

$$
R({t}_{1})=1\,000.
$$

We solve the above equation for ${t}_{1},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}1\,000 & =20\,000{e}^{-0.25{t}_{1}} \\ \frac{1\,000}{20\,000} & ={e}^{-0.25{t}_{1}} \\ 0.05 & ={e}^{-0.25{t}_{1}} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(0.05) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-0.25{t}_{1}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(0.05) & =-0.25{t}_{1} \\ {t}_{1} & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.05)}{-0.25} \\ {t}_{1} & ≈11.982\end{aligned}
$$

Rounding to the nearest integer, we conclude that it takes $12$ minutes for the number of unprocessed records to decrease to $1\,000.$
